correctness.rationale: For a connected Ferrers/chain graph, nested finite neighborhoods make each side-degree class a single twin class. Stable equitable color refinement has the proved dichotomy: a mixed cell forces every adjacent quotient cell to be mixed and balanced; connectedness propagates it globally, while otherwise all stable cells are side-pure. In a pure quotient, cell multiplicities and full/empty between-cell adjacencies reconstruct the graph. In the mixed balanced case, each cell contains one twin class per side of equal size and the equitable neighbor count reconstructs both cross-halves. A positive internal count distinguishes the mixed case. The known C2/color-refinement equivalence then yields relative rigidity. Separately, the two-pebble adjacency/equality response types establish exactly K2, nontrivial stars and nonstars as FO2 classes. Independently checked 671 nested-neighborhood presentations with total order <=11, representing 351 WL signatures, with no nonisomorphic WL collision (finite corroboration).
residual_risks: Finite connected simple uncolored Ferrers graphs with at least one edge; no named bipartition.
Unrestricted C2 and FO2 equivalence only; no bounded-depth or disconnected conclusions.
